description: Surface Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energy on the (111) Surface of CeO2 (Fluorite, Fm-3m)
user_prompt: Compute the formation energy of a surface oxygen vacancy on the CeO2(111) surface (fluorite structure, Fm-3m). Optimize both the clean slab and the slab with one surface O removed, then compute E_vf = E(defective) - E(clean) + 1/2 * E(O2). Report E_vf in eV.

references: Ganduglia-Pirovano, Da Silva & Sauer, Phys. Rev. Lett. 102, 026101 (2009)
Han, Zhang, Liu, Ganduglia-Pirovano & Gao, Front. Chem. 7, 436 (2019)
method.modeling: Fluorite CeO2(111), non-polar O-Ce-O trilayer termination; slab of >= 3 trilayers (bottom trilayer fixed), vacuum >= 15 A, >= 2x2x1 surface cell. Remove one outermost (surface) O, relax both clean and defective slabs.
method.rationale: Value 2.3 eV is the surface O-vacancy formation energy on CeO2(111) at PBE+U from Han et al. 2019 (U_eff=5.0 eV). CRITICAL: removing one O leaves two electrons that MUST localize onto two Ce 4f states (Ce^4+ -> Ce^3+); plain PBE without +U delocalizes them and gives a qualitatively wrong result. The +/-0.30 eV tolerance spans the U-value dependence, the Ce^3+ localization pattern, supercell/slab-thickness differences, and the ~0.4 eV PBE O2 overbinding error. Subsurface vacancies are ~0.2-0.5 eV more stable than surface ones, so the prompt pins the SURFACE vacancy explicitly. ISPIN=2 is required so the reduced slab can localize the Ce^3+ polarons.
